basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 31.' and it opens 'Vers. 31. Tulerunt tunicam ejus. Tunica Joseph caro est Christi, quam de Virgine sumpsit'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text:
Vers. 31. Tulerunt tunicam ejus. Tunica Joseph caro est Christi, quam de Virgine sumpsit et variis virtutum figuris decoravit. Hanc in sanguine haedi tinxerunt, quando invidiam peccati ei facere voluerunt, accusantes eum apud praesidem quasi seditiosum et commoventem populum.

Vers 32, 33. Hanc invenimus, usque, fera pessima | devoravit eum. Planctus iste Jacob propheticus plus dolet de Judaeorum perditione quam de filii sui Joseph, ut putabat, morte. Fera autem pessima populus erat Judaeorum, de quibus olim Psalmista: Filii hominum, dentes eorum arma et sagittae (Psal. LVI, 5).
